_comment: Spike fixture, not a canonical ADR-0001 document. Adaptations, all of them
presentation-only and all of them additive:
1. This top-level '_comment' key and the per-block '_comment' keys are NOT
part of the ADR-0001 envelope or the {type,id,config,slots} node shape.
A strict StatifierBlocks.Document.from_json/1 would need them stripped.
They exist so the spike's fixtures document themselves without a README.
2. Written pretty-printed with keys in reading order (type, id, type_version,
config, slots). ADR-0001 decision 8's canonical form is byte-sorted and
whitespace-free; that form is the encoder's output, not what a human edits.
3. Empty slots are omitted and leaf blocks carry no 'slots' key, which DOES
follow decision 8.
4. No floats anywhere (decision 6): money is integer minor units, durations
are ISO-8601 strings.
Block types: the seven core.* types this document uses from
StatifierBlocks.Core are real. Three more core.* types here are NOT - they
are proposed descriptors in spike/js/proposed-core.js, registered beside the
real ones so the spike can show what the vocabulary would look like if it
grew them: core.invoke (an outcome slot, blk_cp_authorize and blk_cp_capture),
core.timeout (an interrupt rule on the clock, blk_cp_authz_timeout) and
core.assign (a datamodel write, blk_cp_review_cleared). Every
myapp.* type is a demo palette entry the spike registers; three of them exist
because the core set has no equivalent - see the '_comment' on each first use.
The single deliberately-unresolvable type is myapp.legacy_check (blk_cp_legacy).
Both failure idioms are present on purpose, so one document can be read for
the comparison: idiom A is core.invoke's on_error SLOT (blk_cp_authorize with
a park-and-notify sequence, blk_cp_capture with a lone park), and idiom B is
the predicate branch (blk_cp_capture_retry), which is left exactly as it was.
Shape: 46 blocks, maximum nesting depth 7 (root = depth 1).
Every datamodel path named in a 'cond' resolves in ../datamodel.json.

metadata.name: Card processing
metadata.description: Intake, validation, a three-lane authorization group with interrupts, an outcome branch with capture retry and manual review, and a receipt tail. The authorize and capture calls carry on_error subtrees, so the slot idiom and the retry-predicate idiom can be read side by side.

arm_valid._comment: Depth 3. The authorization group: body holds the lanes and the authorize call, interrupts hold two guarded rules.

lane_fraud_review._comment: Depth 5. A nested group inside a lane: its own body, its own interrupt rail.

arm_low_risk._comment: THE UNRESOLVABLE BLOCK (ADR-0005 decision 12). No palette in the spike registers myapp.legacy_check, so it must render with unavailable chrome, a :block finding, its config read-only as JSON, and its bytes preserved on save. It is deliberately at depth 7 so the case is exercised deep in the tree rather than at the top.

config.label: Tell ops the rating was inconclusive

lane_three_ds._comment: The on-event-plus-timeout idiom: a group whose whole body is a wait, with the completion event on its interrupt rail. The wait is the timeout; the event is the happy path.

body._comment: FAILURE IDIOM A, and the PROPOSED type core.invoke (spike/js/proposed-core.js) - not a shipped core type. The error path is a SLOT the block type declares (umbrella D13, 2026-08-28), so the failure edge is a parent/slot/child relationship like every other edge and the connector stays rendered rather than authored. Idiom B is blk_cp_capture_retry further down: the same kind of failure handled by a predicate the author writes. Three things the rework gave up, all Phase-B findings and none of them decided here: (1) RESOLVED by sb-jvz - core.invoke declared no 'label' field, so the 'label' below was stored data the canvas titled the card from while the inspector form could not edit it; the editor injects 'label' into every block type's config schema now, and no type declares one; (2) myapp.authorize's 'timeout' key has no core.invoke equivalent, so it is dropped rather than carried as undeclared config - the authorization timeout already lives on this group's interrupt rail as blk_cp_authz_timeout, which is where a timeout belongs; (3) type_version drops from 2 to 1, because core.invoke's currentVersion is 1 and a stored version above the descriptor's is a hard block_type_too_new refusal. FOURTH, resolved by sb-c2o 2026-08-28: assign_to read 'authorization', a path ../datamodel.json never declared (sb-ig4's finding), while this run's deltas and the outcome branch's guards both spoke of auth.*. It now names 'auth', which the datamodel does declare - the same fact, spelled once. That makes this block the worked example for the declaration check rather than its first warning; the surviving undeclared case is signup-invitations' core.subchart, left deliberately.

on_error._comment: Depth 5. The on_error slot is zero_or_one, so a failure path of more than one step needs a container - a sequence here, and the two steps sit at depth 6.

interrupts._comment: The guarded interrupt rule, authored on the CORE form since 2026-08-28 (sb-0o4, umbrella D12). It used to be myapp.guarded_on_event - a demo type that existed only because core.on_event carried no condition - and the spike proved the affordance was worth it, so core.on_event grew an optional 'cond' (PROPOSED, flagged at the descriptor in spike/js/palette.js) and the crutch was retired. The stored config did not move: event, cond and outcome are spelled exactly as they were, and only the type name changed. Whether the key earns an ADR-0002 amendment is still a Phase-B finding, not something this fixture decides.

The PT15M authorization timeout, authored on the PROPOSED core type core.timeout (spike/js/proposed-core.js) since 2026-08-28 (sb-0o4, umbrella D12) - not a shipped core type. It used to be myapp.timeout_rule, a demo type that existed because no core type expressed 'interrupt this group after a duration': core.wait is a step inside a body, not a rule on an interrupt rail. The stored config did not move - after, cond and outcome are spelled exactly as they were - which is the argument for the proposal: the core form covers what the host form was standing in for, key for key.

config.label: Tell the customer what was wrong

arms.cond: auth.approved AND fraud.cleared AND balance.available_cents >= amount_cents

body._comment: FAILURE IDIOM A in its minimal shape: the on_error slot holding one leaf step rather than a container. Idiom B sits directly below it, and this pair is the comparison the document exists to make. The predicate branch can only see failures the datamodel records (auth.captured == false, capture_attempts < 3); the on_error slot catches the ones it cannot, including the call never answering at all. Neither idiom subsumes the other, which is why both are kept here rather than one replacing the other. 'amount_key' is gone: params carries the same fact as a name/path binding, which is what core.invoke declares. sb-e2x 2026-08-28: params is stored as a MAP of name to datamodel path rather than as one name=path-per-line string - the text field was a flagged compromise and it is gone from the stored bytes, not just from the control.

FAILURE IDIOM B, unchanged from before the rework and deliberately so: the retry idiom is a one-armed branch whose arm is a wait-then-repeat sequence, and its guard is an ordinary condition the author wrote. Read it beside the on_error slot above - same failure, one edge declared by the block type and one edge derived from the datamodel.

Left on the host type on purpose, where the first capture moved to core.invoke. Two reasons, both about what the document has to keep proving: the retry idiom reads honestly only if the block inside it is the block a host writes today, and myapp.capture is the one type in the palette pointing at its own accent token (--sb-accent-myapp-capture, overridden in css/themes/host-brand.css), so this is the last instance of the accent-layering demo on the canvas. A pass that converted it too would delete both without saying so.

arm_manual_review._comment: The park / needs-attention idiom inside a resumable group with deep history: the work parks, a human resolves it days later, and re-entry lands back where it stopped.

body._comment: The PROPOSED type core.assign (spike/js/proposed-core.js), added 2026-08-28 (sb-y4a) - not a shipped core type. It is here rather than anywhere else because this is the one place in the document where the chart itself knows a fact the host does not: the reviewer has answered, so the work is no longer parked, and until now nothing in the vocabulary could write that down. Read it against blk_cp_manual_resolved on this group's interrupt rail, whose guard tests 'review.parked' - the flag that rule reads is a flag a block can now set, which is the argument for the type in one line. 'value' is SOURCE TEXT ('false', not a boolean), the same rule every delta in ../runs.json holds to, and run_cp_manual_review's last step carries that exact pair as its delta.
